history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, temple, or map source documents a specific 'Gopinath Mandir' in Tamenglong town or district; this entry is provisional (verify). The name is generic - there are many Gopinath Mandirs across India (West Bengal, Assam, Tripura, Vrindavan and others all surfaced in searches). The best-documented Gopinath shrine in Manipur is the large Shree Gopinath Mandir at Ningthoukhong in Bishnupur district (described by tourism sources as the second-largest Hindu temple in Manipur, drawing large festival crowds) - but it is a different temple roughly 100+ km away and must NOT be treated as this row's referent without evidence. Tamenglong district is overwhelmingly Christian (Naga Baptist), and any Hindu shrine in the town would be a small community temple of the non-tribal population with no published record. Treat all details here as provisional pending local verification.

town_description: Tamenglong is the headquarters town of Tamenglong district in western Manipur, a Naga-majority hill town at about 1,290 m elevation in the Barak river basin. It is known for its oranges, the nearby Zeilad Lake, Tharon cave and Buning meadows. The district is overwhelmingly Christian (Baptist), so Hindu shrines here, if any, are small community temples serving the non-tribal population rather than historic pilgrimage sites.
